audit_findings.mechanism: Future equity-funded growth increases aggregate OE, but shares issued beyond the 219.117507 million denominator reduce OE and value per current share.
audit_findings.evidence: It is anticipated that all of the funds required for capital expenditures for the years 2026 through 2028 will be funded by various sources, including equity issuance, debt financing and internally generated funds.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that equity is an intended capital-plan funding source and that substantial unused issuance capacity exists. It does not establish how much additional equity will be issued or whether its proceeds and incremental earnings were modeled. The error is therefore not demonstrated, but dilution on the filed capacity's scale is reasonably capable of materially changing per-share value.
audit_findings.action: Build an annual 2026-2028 financing schedule covering the remaining FSAs, ATM issuance and other equity; add issued shares and proceeds to each scenario, then rerun per-share values and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized interest may violate the equity-OE rail
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.726 million in 2025 AFUDC—$7.425 million borrowed and $2.301 million equity—equal to 9.0% of the $108.1 million OE anchor; 2026 first-half borrowed AFUDC was $4.1 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Unsubtracted borrowed AFUDC omits a financing cash cost from equity-level OE, while retained equity AFUDC adds noncash income to the OE numerator.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company is permitted to capitalize AFUDC on regulated construction projects and to include such amounts in rate base when the related facilities are placed in service.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed amounts demonstrate material AFUDC activity, but the record does not show the valuation adjustments well enough to prove either component was mishandled. The 2025 amount is large relative to the OE anchor, so an omission could materially overstate operating value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each OE year from filed net income and cash flow to the valuation numerator; identify the treatment of borrowed AFUDC in maintenance capex and remove equity AFUDC income, then rerun all scenarios if either component remains in OE.

audit_findings.title: Asset-retirement claims may sit ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $441.048 million gross ARO at 2026-06-30, equal to $2.01 per diluted share and 28.2% of the $1.565 billion base equity value; economically unrecoverable net amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any ARO settlement not recovered from customers or otherwise funded reduces future OE or requires a direct senior-claim deduction in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At December 31, 2025, the Company had total liabilities of $431.9 million related to asset retirement obligations that are excluded from the table above.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligation is demonstrated and is large relative to base equity value. The filing states that largely all regulated ARO expenses are expected to be recovered in rates, but it does not establish complete, timely recovery of every obligation. Thus the gross liability is not itself the valuation error, while an unrecovered portion remains capable of materially reducing value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $441.048 million ARO by asset and jurisdiction to regulatory assets, removal-cost regulatory liabilities, insurance, customer funding and approved recovery; model settlement timing in OE or deduct the present value of the unrecoverable net amount.

audit_findings.title: Historical OE may cross the spin-off perimeter
audit_findings.mechanism: Including Knife River or Everus in 2016-2021 OE would create an artificial decline when calibrating growth for the current utility-and-pipeline perimeter; the $108.1 million latest-year anchor itself is protected by the MIN(trend, latest) rule.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of the separations, the historical results of operations are shown in discontinued operations, net of tax, except for allocated general corporate overhead costs of the Company, which did not meet the criteria for discontinued operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The filings demonstrate that the spun businesses are presented as discontinued operations for the comparative periods supplied, but they do not establish how the valuation reconstructed the older OE observations. If older figures retain the spun businesses, treating the decline as deterioration would bias growth downward. Because the valuation anchors to 2025 OE rather than the higher trend, the possible effect is confined mainly to growth calibration and cannot be quantified from the record.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2016-2021 OE on the present MDU perimeter, excluding Knife River and Everus while retaining stranded corporate costs; document whether the bear, base and bull growth rates change and rerun them if they do.

audit_findings.title: Spin-off tax exposure is an unmodeled contingent senior claim
audit_findings.mechanism: A tax assessment borne by MDU would reduce cash available to common equity through a probability-weighted bridge deduction or future OE outflow.
audit_findings.evidence: In the event the IRS were to prevail in such challenge, the Company and its stockholders could be subject to significant U.S. federal income tax liability.
audit_findings.explanation: The completed separations create a continuing contingent exposure, but no assessment, probability or loss range is supplied. IRS private-letter rulings and tax opinions reduce apparent risk without eliminating it. The record therefore cannot establish either an error or materiality, although a successful challenge could reduce value.
audit_findings.action: Review the separation agreements, tax indemnities, representations, continuing undertakings and current compliance certifications; identify which entity bears each exposure and quantify a probability-weighted adjustment if loss is more than remote.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge may include unavailable restricted cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $46.269 million maximum bridge exposure, equal to $0.21 per diluted share; the 2026-06-30 restricted portion is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Restricted or required operating cash should be excluded from the cash-and-STI addition to the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Restricted cash represents deposits held by the Company’s captive insurance company that is required by state insurance regulations to remain in the captive insurance company.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest balance-sheet caption combines cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash, so adding the full $46.269 million as distributable cash is a demonstrated classification error unless a separate reconciliation was performed. Even if none of the amount were distributable, the maximum effect is about 3.0% of the $7.14 base value and 4.2% of the $5.00 buy-below price, which cannot change the conclusion relative to the $19.57 market price.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 2026 cash-footnote reconciliation, remove captive-insurer restricted deposits and a supported minimum operating-cash amount from the bridge, and update value per share without changing operating assumptions.
